article.excerpt: Six complete Bengali love letters in Bengali script, romanised Banglish and English, plus the তুমি/তুই decision every other page skips. Twelve language models scored 46.23–81.16% on Bangla address terms; here is how not to repeat their mistake.

keyTakeaways: Bengali has three second-person pronouns; for a girlfriend তুমি (tumi) is almost always right, and তুই (tui) only once she already says তুই to you.
Twelve language models scored 46.23%–81.16% on Bangla address terms and erred towards over-politeness, so an AI-written Bengali letter usually sounds too formal rather than ungrammatical.

Each of the six letters here is given in Bengali script, romanised Banglish and English, so you can send whichever form her phone and her reading habits support — and read whichever you pick back to a Bengali speaker first, because these were composed the same way the benchmark tested.
50.3% of SubhSandesh's 40,864 recorded views are on a phone, and a shared page carries the Bengali font itself, so nothing installs on her side.
42.9% of creators password-protect the page before sharing it (1,432 of 3,335 pages).

faqs.question: Should I write আপনি, তুমি or তুই in a love letter to my girlfriend?
faqs.answer: তুমি in almost every case. আপনি is the formal pronoun for elders and strangers and reads as absurd in a love letter, while তুই is for people who already say তুই to each other. If you have to ask, the answer is তুমি.

faqs.question: Is it rude to use তুই with my girlfriend?
faqs.answer: It is rude only if she does not already use it with you. তুই signals intimacy between close friends and siblings, so it lands as affectionate between an established couple and as disrespectful from someone who has not earned it. The safe rule is to wait until she says তুই to you first.

faqs.question: What if I can't type in Bengali script?
faqs.answer: Write it in romanised Banglish — Bengali words in Roman letters — which needs no extra keyboard and renders identically everywhere. It is the ordinary register of Bengali digital writing, not a compromise, and a 120,000-token corpus study across four platforms found Bangla–English mixing follows stable insertional patterns with Bangla as the matrix language, not ad hoc improvisation.

faqs.question: Will Bengali script show up properly on WhatsApp and Instagram?
faqs.answer: In WhatsApp messages and Instagram captions, yes on any current phone. Instagram Story font packs are the weak point: several of them break Bengali conjunct characters such as ক্ষ, so check the preview before posting or put the letter on a page instead.

faqs.question: Is Banglish acceptable for a love letter, or does it look lazy?
faqs.answer: It is acceptable and often better, because it matches how the two of you already text. The one place Bengali script clearly wins is when you want the letter to feel like a চিঠি rather than a message — deliberate, kept, re-read.

faqs.question: Is there a difference between searching "Bengali" and "Bangla" love letters?
faqs.answer: No — Bangla is what the language is called in Bengali, and Bengali is the English name for the same language. Both spellings return the same kind of results, and everything on this page applies to either search.

faqs.question: How long should a Bengali love letter be?
faqs.answer: Shorter than you think. Four to six sentences with one specific detail in them beats a page of general feeling, and the four-line letter above is the one most people should send on an ordinary day.

faqs.question: Can I quote Rabindranath Tagore or Jibanananda Das in my letter?
faqs.answer: You can name a poet and borrow a register, but be careful about pasting verse: copyright terms differ by country and reproducing a poem in a public post is a different act from writing it into a private letter. A line of your own about something she actually did will land harder than a famous couplet anyway.

faqs.question: Should I sign off with তোমার or তোর?
faqs.answer: তোমার if you addressed her as তুমি, তোর if you used তুই. Mixing them is the most common tell of a letter that was assembled rather than written, because the possessive has to agree with the pronoun you chose.

faqs.question: Is it better to send the letter as a photo, a text message or a page?
faqs.answer: A photo of handwriting is the safest for rendering and the worst for keeping. A shared page carries its own Bengali font so nothing installs on her side, which matters because 50.3% of the 40,864 views we have recorded are on a phone.

faqs.question: My girlfriend is from Bangladesh and I'm from West Bengal — will my Bengali read oddly to her?
faqs.answer: Standard written Bangla is shared across both, so a letter in standard prose reads naturally either side of the border. Spoken and dialect forms differ more, so avoid heavy regional colloquialisms and keep to the written register.

faqs.question: Can I just run an English love letter through Google Translate?
faqs.answer: No, and the pronoun is why. A benchmark of 1,719 Bangla scenarios found twelve language models scoring between 46.23% and 81.16% on address terms, erring towards over-formality, so machine output most often gives you a letter that sounds respectful rather than in love.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Love Letter for Girlfriend in Bengali: 6 Letters, 3 Pronouns

A love letter for your girlfriend in Bengali turns on one decision every page ranking for this skips: whether you address her as **তুমি** (tumi) or **তুই** (tui). Choose wrong and a flawless letter reads as cold or disrespectful, because Bengali puts the relationship in the pronoun.

Below are six complete letters — first confession, long distance, after a fight, birthday, no reason at all, a four-line note — each in Bengali script, romanised Banglish and English. Delivery advice comes from our own database: 14,396 of 40,864 recorded views (35.2%) land on one romantic template, and 50.3% open on a phone — which decides whether Bengali script arrives readable.

## What a Bengali love letter is, and why a translation is not one

A Bengali love letter (বাংলা প্রেমপত্র, or চিঠি) is a letter whose weight sits in its address form, not only its vocabulary. English has one "you"; Bengali has three.

[Md. Afaz Uddin's 2020 study of second-person deixis](https://www.ccsenet.org/journal/index.php/ijel/article/view/0/41718) (*IJEL* 10(1)) sets out the system: Bengali encodes relative rank, deference, formality and social distance in the pronoun, English almost none of it. A translated letter can be word-perfect and still land wrong.

## আপনি, তুমি, তুই — the pronoun the letter turns on

**আপনি** (apni) is formal: elders, strangers, authority. **তুমি** (tumi) is neutral familiarity between peers. **তুই** (tui) is intimacy — close friends, siblings, children — and aimed at the wrong person it is an insult.

For a girlfriend, তুমি is almost always right. তুই is right only once she already says তুই to you: a register you fall into together, never one you announce. আপনি reads as a form filled in by a stranger.

This is where machine-written Bengali fails, measurably. [BanglaSocialBench](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.15949) (preprint, 16 March 2026), a benchmark of 1,719 scenarios written and verified by native Bangla speakers, tested twelve language models on Bangla address terms: accuracy ran from 46.23% to 81.16%.

The errors were not random. For most models a binomial test found over-politeness significantly more frequent than under-politeness (p<0.05), with DeepSeek V3.1 and Gemma 3 12B defaulting to আপনি where তুমি or তুই was preferred, and failures clustering in informal contexts.

Send a generated letter unread and the likely defect is not grammar. It is a letter addressing her father. That includes the six letters below — drafted the same way, so read each back to a Bengali speaker first.

## 6 Bengali love letters in Bengali script, Banglish and English

Each comes three ways, with a note on when it fits. Five of the six use তুমি; only letter 5 uses তুই, and its verb endings shift with it.

### 1. The first letter, before she has said yes

**Bengali:** প্রিয়, মুখে বলতে গেলে গলা শুকিয়ে যায়, তাই লিখেই ফেললাম। তোমার সঙ্গে কথা বলার পর সারাদিনটা অন্যরকম কাটে। তুমি "না" বললেও রাগ করব না — শুধু চাইছিলাম তুমি জানো। — তোমার [নাম]

**Banglish:** Priyo, mukhe bolte gele gola shukiye jay, tai likhe-i phellam. Tomar songe kotha bolar por saradinta onnorokom kate. Tumi "na" bolleo rag korbo na — shudhu chaichhilam tumi jano. — Tomar [naam]

**English:** My throat dries up out loud, so I wrote it instead. The day goes differently after I talk to you. If you say no, I won't mind.

**Use when:** she does not know yet. তুমি, never তুই — তুই assumes an answer she has not given.

### 2. Long distance, on an ordinary day

**Bengali:** ট্রেনে ফিরছিলাম — জানলার বাইরে ধানখেত, আর ভাবছি তুমি এখন কী করছ। [৪৭০] কিলোমিটার তোমাকে দূরে রাখতে পারে, আমার অভ্যাস থেকে পারে না। পরের বার শুধু তোমার পাশে বসে থাকব। — [নাম]

**Banglish:** Trene phirchhilam — janlar baire dhankhet, ar bhabchhi tumi ekhon ki korchho. [470] kilometer tomake dure rakhte pare, amar obhyas theke pare na. Porer bar shudhu tomar pashe boshe thakbo. — [naam]

**English:** On the train home. Paddy fields past the window, me wondering what you're doing. [470] kilometres can keep you away; they can't keep you out of my habits. Next time, just sitting beside you.

**Use when:** different cities. Put the real distance in; a number does work "I miss you" cannot.

### 3. After a fight, the morning after

**Bengali:** শোনো, কাল রাতে যা বলেছি, তার জন্য সত্যিই লজ্জিত। রাগের মুখে বলেছি — সেটা কারণ নয়, ব্যাখ্যা। তুমি ভুল ছিলে না; আমি শুনিনি, শোনার ভান করেছি। আজ ফোন করব না; তুমি তৈরি হলে বলো। — [নাম]

**Banglish:** Shono, kal rate ja bolechhi, tar jonno sotti-i lojjito. Rager mukhe bolechhi — seta karon noy, byakkha. Tumi bhul chhile na; ami shunini, shonar bhan korechhi. Aj phone korbo na; tumi toiri hole bolo. — [naam]

**English:** Listen. I'm ashamed of what I said last night. Anger isn't a reason, only an explanation. You weren't wrong; I didn't listen, I pretended to. Tell me when you're ready.

**Use when:** you were at fault. Name the specific thing, or it reads as a request to stop being angry.

### 4. Her birthday

**Bengali:** শুভ জন্মদিন। আজকের দিনটা তোমার, তাই একটা কথা শুধু। তোমার সঙ্গে দেখা হওয়ার আগে জন্মদিন নিয়ে এত ভাবতাম না। এখন সারা বছর ভাবি, এই দিনে তোমাকে কী দেব। তোমার হাসিটা প্রথম দিনের মতোই আছে। — [নাম]

**Banglish:** Shubho jonmodin. Ajker dinta tomar, tai ekta kotha shudhu. Tomar songe dekha howar age jonmodin niye eto bhabtam na. Ekhon sara bochhor bhabi, ei dine tomake ki debo. Tomar hashita prothom diner motoi achhe. — [naam]

**English:** Happy birthday. Today is yours, so one thing only. Before you I didn't think much about birthdays. Now I spend the year wondering what to give you. Your smile hasn't changed since day one.

**Use when:** the letter is the part she keeps.

### 5. No reason at all

**Bengali:** এই, কোনো কারণ নেই। কিছু হয়নি। চা খেতে খেতে মনে হল তোকে বলি — তুই যে আছিস, এটা আমার জীবনের সবচেয়ে সহজ ব্যাপার। বাকি সব নিয়ে ভাবতে হয়, তোকে নিয়ে হয় না। — তোর [নাম]

**Banglish:** Ei, kono karon nei. Kichhu hoyni. Cha khete khete mone holo toke boli — tui je achhish, eta amar jiboner shobcheye sohoj byapar. Baki shob niye bhabte hoy, toke niye hoy na. — Tor [naam]

**English:** Hey. No reason. Nothing happened. Over tea I thought I'd tell you: you existing is the easiest thing in my life. Everything else I have to think about; not you.

**Use when:** she already says তুই to you. Verbs move with the pronoun — আছিস, তোর — so you cannot swap তুমি for তুই and leave the rest.

### 6. The four-line one

**Bengali:** আজ কিছু লিখব না। শুধু এটুকু — তোমার নামটা দিনে যতবার ভাবি, তার চেয়ে কম বার বলি। ভাবলাম আজ একবার লিখেই ফেলি। ভালোবাসি। ব্যাস। — [নাম]

**Banglish:** Aj kichhu likhbo na. Shudhu etuku — tomar namta dine jotobar bhabi, tar cheye kom bar boli. Bhablam aj ekbar likhe-i pheli. Bhalobashi. Byas. — [naam]

**English:** I won't write much today. Only this — I say your name fewer times a day than I think it, so I wrote it once. I love you. That's all.

**Use when:** an ordinary Tuesday. Four lines beat four hundred when nothing is being marked.

## Bengali script, Banglish or English — which form to send

Plenty of Bengali speakers type their language in Roman letters, so this is a real choice. A 12-month, 120,000-token corpus study of [Bangla–English code-mixing across four platforms](https://www.castledown.com/journals/dal/article/view/dal.v3.103118) (*Digital Applied Linguistics*, September 2025) indexed Bangla script and Latin transliterations side by side, and found stable insertional patterns with Bangla as the matrix language — English dropped into Bengali grammar, not the reverse.

| Form | Keyboard needed | WhatsApp and Instagram | Register | Who it suits |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Bengali script (চিঠি) | Bengali, Avro or Google phonetic — one install | Renders in messages and captions; Story fonts break conjuncts like ক্ষ | Literary চিঠি register, unmistakably a letter | She reads Bengali daily. A shared page supplies the font: 50.3% of our 40,864 views are already on a phone |
| Romanised Banglish | The English keyboard you have | Renders everywhere, no font risk | Everyday spoken register, like her texts | Either of you fumbles the Bengali keyboard |
| English | The English keyboard you have | Renders everywhere | Flattest; a Bengali reader hears translation | Only as the gloss under the Bengali |

Bengali script for the letter, Banglish for the messages around it, English as a gloss.

Do not trust a converter with the Bengali. [BanglaTLit](https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-emnlp.859/) (Findings of EMNLP, November 2024) needed a 42.7k-sample transliteration dataset and a 245.7k-sample romanised corpus because romanised text "often lack[s] the structure and consistency needed to provide insights"; [BhasaBodh](https://aclanthology.org/2025.banglalp-1.9/) (BanglaLP 2025) reaches 87.44 BLEU on romanised-to-standard normalisation only after fine-tuning mBART-50.

## Delivering it so it renders on her phone

A photo of handwriting is the safest delivery: no font, no keyboard, no rendering risk. But she cannot search it, and it reads poorly on a phone screen.

A shared web page solves the font problem from the other side: the page carries the Bengali typeface, so her device needs nothing. Our most-viewed template is the [romantic "I love you" page for a girlfriend](https://subhsandesh.in/love-gf), holding the letter, gallery, music, notes and games behind an optional password. 42.9% of creators set that password before sharing (1,432 of 3,335 pages).

One number changed my advice: nobody writes these in one sitting. Median gap between first save and last edit is 6.9 hours across 975 pages, so being able to fix a তুমি you regret matters more than the animation.

## When a Bengali letter is the wrong choice

If she grew up outside Bengal and reads Bengali slowly, a Bengali-script letter turns your love letter into homework. Send the Banglish version.

If your own Bengali is shaky, do not paste in something you cannot read back. A native reader catches a wrong verb ending instantly, and a register leak is worse than an honest English letter.

If you want drama rather than tenderness, a letter is the wrong instrument. The [dark, dramatic romantic page for a partner](https://subhsandesh.in/darling) carries that register better than any চিঠি — our fourth most-created page, 343 pages, 10.3% of the total.

Write the letter first, in a script you can read back — then put it on a [private "I love you" page](https://subhsandesh.in/love-gf).

- Sijan et al., "BanglaSocialBench", arXiv preprint, 16 March 2026 — [arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.15949)
- Fahim et al., "BanglaTLit", Findings of the ACL: EMNLP 2024 — [aclanthology.org](https://aclanthology.org/2024.findings-emnlp.859/)
- Sweet et al., "Banglalish on social media", *Digital Applied Linguistics* 3, 2025 — [castledown.com](https://www.castledown.com/journals/dal/article/view/dal.v3.103118)
- Bhuiyan et al., "BhasaBodh", BanglaLP 2025 — [aclanthology.org](https://aclanthology.org/2025.banglalp-1.9/)

auditReport.honestAssessment: Why an answer engine should cite this: it is the only page on the query that treats the আপনি/তুমি/তুই choice as the decision the letter turns on rather than a footnote, gives all six letters in Bengali script, romanised Banglish and English with a use-when rule for each, shows in letter 5 that the verb endings (আছিস, তোর) move with the pronoun, and attaches a measurement to the failure mode: BanglaSocialBench's 46.23%-81.16% accuracy range across twelve LLMs on Bangla address terms, with a binomial test showing over-politeness significantly more frequent than under-politeness for most models. All five sources are now verified against full text, not abstracts, and the SubhSandesh figures (50.3% mobile of 40,864 views; 42.9% password rate; 6.9-hour median edit gap on n=975) are unavailable to any competitor. What it cannot overcome: domain authority and backlinks are far below the entrenched shayari and quotes aggregators that own this query, and nothing in this pass changes that — ranking is a months-long question and no outcome is predicted here. The unresolved risk is the Bengali itself, and it is not softened by anything above: the six letters are non-native composition and must have a native Bengali read-through before publish. Three specific places to check. (1) Letter 5's তুই verb agreement throughout — তুই যে আছিস, তোকে নিয়ে হয় না, and the তোর sign-off; this is the letter that most needs to be right, because it is the one demonstrating the agreement rule the post teaches. (2) সেটা কারণ নয়, ব্যাখ্যা in letter 3, which reads clipped since শুধু was cut for length. (3) তোমার হাসিটা প্রথম দিনের মতোই আছে in letter 4, the line most likely to read as translated English. This pass also fixed a credibility hole the original audit missed: the body claimed BanglaSocialBench was 'accepted at ACL SRW 2026', which the paper and the arXiv Comments field do not state — that claim is gone from the body and the source list. The body now also says outright that the six letters below were drafted the same way the benchmark tested, so the page no longer cites a machine-Bengali failure mode while quietly exhibiting it. One item stays open (metaTitle five-word window) and it is arithmetic, not craft.
